_doc: The regulars layer (world v58) — 'the house knows.' Per-venue registry of the people whose order starts before they sit down: standing order, usual window, usual spot, the surface facts the counter carries about them, first-name basis, and tab status. Companion spec: world/regulars.md. Demo: world/regulars.html (inline REG mirror, hand-synced). Machine consumers: the brain/prompt layer (counter-side texture), the crowd/wire layers (who is likely where, when). Rules: every fact is SURFACE knowledge — things a counter worker could plausibly know, same bar as a possession briefing; no secrets, no seeds, no Mission Unfiltered. Tabs are game dollars. Regulars exist only for door tiers (anchor + street); a venue's own staff are never its regulars; name_basis ⊆ the venue's staff.

window_keys.days: list of dow abbrevs, or 'daily'; 'weekday' = mon–fri
window_keys.hours: [open, close] in world-clock hours, may cross midnight (e.g. [24, 25.5] = 00:00–01:30)

mudhaus.order: one drip — occupied for two hours, refills declined politely
house_knows: Tuesday is hers — the table gets held without being asked
cash, exact change, counted twice at the counter
hemming talk is welcome; small talk before the first refill is not

mudhaus.order: a latte, then a second one nobody sees her order
house_knows: headphones on means do-not-disturb — staff run interference on chatty strangers
the outlet chair is hers by tenure; new laptops get steered elsewhere

mudhaus.order: two drips to go — one for the guy on the scaffold next door
house_knows: in and out before the rush — never waits, never has to
tips like it's a union rule

mudhaus.order: oat latte and whichever pastry is oldest
mudhaus.spot: the bench end nearest the door
house_knows: straight off a night shift — decaf after nine is automatic, unasked
nobody asks how the shift was; that's the service

el-farolote.order: three al pastor, no cilantro, extra napkins
house_knows: orders in Spanish, answers in monosyllables — both are fluent
the napkin stack is a running joke both sides honor

el-farolote.order: the post-set burrito — carnitas, on the house half the time
el-farolote.spot: the counter end by the register
house_knows: never orders before 1 AM on gig nights — the burrito is the encore
plays the counter like a tip jar; the staff let him

el-farolote.order: two tacos, whatever protein is cheapest that day
el-farolote.spot: the corner table facing the door
house_knows: counts coins on the table before ordering — nobody rushes him
the door-facing seat: he watches the bikes out the glass

auerbach.order: nothing — the hardware-store lunch talk is the purchase
auerbach.spot: the paint-stained end of the counter
house_knows: buys a box of screws to be polite — the screws are not the point
the site next door sends him; Victor knows the lunch break to the minute

auerbach.order: buttons, zippers, and the occasional lamp part
house_knows: brings her own tape measure — the shop's is decorative to her
Victor prices notions like a neighbor, not a shopkeeper; both pretend otherwise
the left table is hers and Ray's by tenure — staff wave her through the line on packed days
fog and rain move her inside without a word; the first clear afternoon moves her back

dolores-perk.order: coffee, black, plus a bread-crust pocket for the pigeons
dolores-perk.spot: the left park-side table, across from Esther
house_knows: pigeon crumbs are tolerated to exactly one table's worth
he argues the park's politics with Esther; the volume is the regularity

dolores-perk.order: a water refill and a banana
dolores-perk.spot: standing at the rail — he never sits
house_knows: the rail is his stretch spot; the lap count is written in his legs

buy-rite-market.order: the week's list — one cart, Tuesday night
house_knows: price-checks the peaches every week like it's a ritual
checkout staff know her tote by sight

buy-rite-market.order: ingredients priced like a man doing math in his head
buy-rite-market.spot: the meat case, then the spice aisle
house_knows: compares every price against Valencia Growers — you can watch him decide
asks the butcher questions a home cook doesn't ask

buy-rite-market.spot: in and out — the basket never fills
house_knows: the coin purse is older than most of the staff
declines bags; brings her own, folded flat as an envelope

buy-rite-creamery.order: a single scoop, whatever the special is
buy-rite-creamery.spot: the bench, homework on her knees
house_knows: the scoop is a sometimes-thing — she reads the line's rhythm before joining it
school bag stays on; she's between the bus and home

buy-rite-creamery.order: whatever's cheapest — filmed first, eaten second
house_knows: the forty-minute line is the point for her — it's content, not delay

il-delfino.order: one pasta at the bar, a book she's not really reading
il-delfino.spot: the bar seat nearest the kitchen door
house_knows: the solo Thursday is a standing reservation nobody wrote down
staff keep her water full and her evening undisturbed — that's the whole service

il-delfino.order: the deuce by the window, when the calendar allows
house_knows: the hostess knows not to seat her near the kitchen
industry courtesy runs both directions — she tips like a manager because she is one

baguette-about-it.order: a morning bun, split with Ray on the walk home
baguette-about-it.spot: the counter, then the door — it's a handoff
house_knows: Hana sets one aside when the weekend batch runs small
the split bun is a two-household arrangement the shop honors

baguette-about-it.order: a country loaf, sliced, plus a croissant eaten on the walk
house_knows: off-shift Sundays only — the loaf is the week's bread
sellout is 13:00; she has never once cut it close

the-600-club.order: well whiskey when it's raining, the cheap beer when it isn't
the-600-club.spot: the stage corner — the doorway when it's wet
house_knows: his rain pitch is a standing booking nobody wrote down
the bartender keeps his guitar behind the bar between sets

tab.rule: settles in cash on Sundays and in songs the rest of the week

the-600-club.order: a whiskey ginger at the back booth
house_knows: the booth is hers after tattoo shifts — nobody sits there after ten
she sketches on napkins; the staff keep the good ones behind the bar

the-600-club.order: one beer, nursed past the point of politeness
house_knows: Thursday is the drum circle — Sunday he's just tired
one beer buys him two hours of the game; the bartender's math allows it

dandy-lion.order: one truffle — the treat he can't afford
dandy-lion.spot: the sample tray, then the register
house_knows: he circles twice before buying; the staff pretend not to watch
payday Friday is the only reliable visit

dandy-lion.order: a hot chocolate when it's foggy
house_knows: gray mornings bring her — weather as a habit
whipped cream is declined with ceremony every time

valencia-growers.spot: every stall, in the same order
house_knows: the vendors know he runs a kitchen by the questions he asks
he buys one token case of tomatoes to stay a customer

valencia-growers.order: a walk of the stalls before her own stand opens
valencia-growers.spot: the perimeter first, then the competition
house_knows: her regulars migrate here Saturdays — she prices against them and they know it
the vendors save her the bruised fruit at cost; vendor solidarity outranks rivalry

needlepointe.order: flash — whatever's new on Bex's sheet
house_knows: reads the flash sheet like a setlist
his appointments cluster after good tip weeks — the shop can hear a good week on him

needlepointe.order: the walk-in Saturday consultation — usually hypothetical
house_knows: three consultations, zero tattoos — Bex doesn't push
her chalkboard style and the flash style are cousins; the shop knows it

folsom-auto.order: the van's fluids, cash, no receipt questions
house_knows: the corner-store van is the oldest thing on the block still running
Gus keeps it alive out of professional pride — the invoice is honorary
a bicycle at an auto shop — Gus does it anyway, off the books
the consult is free; the beer run afterward is the fee

maliks.order: an energy drink and the cheapest sandwich
maliks.spot: the counter, half in the doorway
house_knows: Malik starts the sandwich when the scooter pulls up
the between-deliveries ten minutes are his only sit-down

tab.rule: settles Fridays, cash — never once missed

maliks.spot: in and out — thirty seconds, tops
house_knows: post-run hydration is a ritual with a handshake
the exact change is laid out before the bottle leaves the fridge
Malik knows everyone's order — hers is the one he teases
Friday night is her restock; the chalkboard gets sketched at the counter

las-palmas.order: a mango, cut into a flower when Luz has time
house_knows: the fruit-flower is an unpriced courtesy
stoop reports get filed here first — Luz hears the block through Esther

las-palmas.order: the day's bruised fruit, at cost
house_knows: bruised is not a euphemism — she wants it and says so
Luz sets the box aside before the stand opens

las-palmas.order: whatever's overstocked, plus the day-old bananas
house_knows: the bananas are for the pigeons and everybody knows it
he calls her 'hija' — she lets him

bloom-and-doom.order: ribbon ends and the stems Ida can't sell
house_knows: seamstress and florist trade trimmings both directions
Carmen hems Ida's aprons; Ida saves Carmen the odd stems — nobody invoices

bloom-and-doom.order: a single stem for the library desk
bloom-and-doom.spot: mostly the door — she never stays
house_knows: the Monday stem is a budget line she gives herself
Ida picks it; Vera has never once chosen

golden-hour.order: two machines, Thursday morning — the same two
golden-hour.spot: the folding table by the window
house_knows: her machines are known — a stranger in one gets looked at
the bulletin board is her newspaper; she reads it while the dryer runs

golden-hour.order: wash-and-fold drop when the month runs long
house_knows: the Friday-night laundromat date is a genre — Jules is the Sunday-night solo version
she counts quarters on the folding table like a card player

golden-hour.order: scrubs, hot water, nobody talks to her
house_knows: the back row stays quiet for a reason — staff and regulars both keep it
double-load Saturdays after a run of nights

dusty-spine.order: the YA spin rack — borrowed, not bought
dusty-spine.spot: the spin rack, floor if the chair's taken
house_knows: borrowed versus bought is legible in what her tote carries out
the clerk holds new YA arrivals under the counter for an hour
she's the librarian — the free box's order is her doing
the clerk pretends not to notice; the noticing is mutual

marooned.order: one 45 from the dollar bin, every Sunday
marooned.spot: the dollar bin, knees on the floor
house_knows: the Sunday tithe is a standing beat — the clerk pulls the weird ones for him
what the bin teaches him turns up in the park set

marooned.order: sells back the same three records every broke month
house_knows: the clerk keeps a hold shelf — the buy-back is a payday ritual
she buys them back when tips recover; the clerk never mentions it

the-musket.order: one cocktail, two small plates — studied like homework
the-musket.spot: the bar seat with the kitchen sightline
house_knows: he isn't dining, he's researching — the staff know the restaurant in the notebook
the bartender answers his questions because the questions are good

the-musket.order: a walk-in bar seat, one drink, early
house_knows: choosing the Musket over Il Delfino's formality is a statement the staff can read
the industry recognizes its own — the pour is honest and the tab is short
